plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my true value of $36 maximizes my expected profit—I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I pay less than my value, ensuring no negative outcomes. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down in this format.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, while bidding lower reduces my chances of winning profitably. With a value of $8, bidding exactly $8 ensures I only win when profitable (when the second-highest bid is below $8) and never pay more than my value.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, there's no incentive to shade my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. I will bid exactly my value of $44 to maximize expected profit.
